source_row.rationale: Situational awareness — originally studied extensively in aviation and other high-reliability industries — refers to the continuous perception and understanding of one's environment (in this case, a client's clinical status and broader context) to anticipate potential problems and respond effectively, an important concept increasingly emphasized in healthcare patient safety education.
source_row.source_detail: Situation awareness is the outcome of continual monitoring of patient, team, environment and progress; current TeamSTEPPS curriculum; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A nurse maintains ongoing awareness of a client's overall status, subtle changes, and the broader clinical context throughout a shift, allowing early recognition of a developing complication, and a student assumes this is just a personality trait some nurses happen to have rather than a teachable concept.
